nodes.question: How do non-state actors contribute to discussions at COP events?
nodes.answer: Non-state actors contribute informally by sharing expertise, overseeing the progress of Parties, and supporting ambition through side events and informal meetings.
nodes.paragraph: No Title Available DOI: DOI not available FullTextURL: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-025-02254-9 Nature Climate Change nature climate change Articlehttps://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-25-2254-9 Tracing inclusivity at UNFCCC conferences through side events and interest group dynamics Judy Jingwei Xie 1,2 Nora Alessandra Escher 3, Matilda E. Dunn 1, Yurong Yu 1, lain Staffell 1 & Joeri Rogelj 1,2,4 Inclusivity and transparency are the foundations of procedural justice in climate governance. However, concerns persist around the influence of business interest groups at United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conferences of Parties (COPs). COPs have increased in size and complexity, obscuring agendas and organizational relationships. Here we analyse the discourse and networks of actors at COP side events from 2003 to 2023 using machine learning-based topic modelling and social network analysis. We trace how discussions on energy, food and forests have evolved. Focusing on energy topics, we show that fossil fuel lobbyists gain COP access through developed-country business non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and developing-country governments. Their nominators focus on renewable energy and system approaches but are peripheral in the anti-fossil fuel discourse which grew from a collaborative network of environmental NGOs.
